paper.title: Facile synthesis and hydrogen storage application of nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes with bamboo-like structure

defaults.verified_by: Agent B: 53 cells verified, 0 numeric disputes; 2 judgment calls resolved (pore_volume_method unspecified kept by convention; uptake_bound exact per primary table)

notes.matclass: material_class MWCNT: the paper calls these nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes without stating wall number, but the reported 10-20 nm wall thickness is multi-walled and the corpus files doped nanotubes by structural class (cf. HYC-0025, a boron-doped MWCNT)
notes.dopant: nitrogen doping 1.5 at% by XPS (N1s/C1s intensities), confirmed by combustion elemental analysis (N/C atomic ratio ~0.015); residual_metal_element=Fe from the FeCl3 growth catalyst, not quantified by the paper (only a small amount), and the paper attributes part of the uptake to this residual iron
notes.porevol: total_pore_volume_cm3_g is a single-point value from the N2 adsorption volume at P/Po = 0.99; no average pore diameter value is reported (only the method), so pore_volume_method is unspecified and no diameter is recorded
notes.littab: Table 1 is a literature-summary table (hydrogen storage capacities for representative nitrogen-doped carbon materials); only column 1, N-doped CNTs (this work), is this paper's own data and is extracted; its other columns are cited other-author results and are excluded
notes.type1: uptake_type unspecified (exact-word rule): the low-pressure 77 K isotherm (Fig 5a) that yields this value is not labelled excess; only the Fig 5b and Fig 5c isotherms are
notes.type2: uptake_type excess: the high-pressure 77 K isotherm (Fig 5b) is reported as excess uptake
notes.type3: uptake_type excess: the 298 K isotherm (Fig 5c) is the excess hydrogen adsorption isotherm
notes.method1: measured by a volumetric method (Micromeritics ASAP 2020HD88, 0-800 mmHg, 77 K); sample evacuated at 573 K before measurement; sample mass and blank/calibration not stated
notes.methodhp: high-pressure uptake by an intelligent gravimetric analyser (IGA, Hiden Isochem) in static mode, 0-19 bar; degassed in ultrahigh vacuum (1e-6 mbar) at 573 K for 10 h; H2 99.999%; sample mass and buoyancy/blank correction not stated

S1.label: N-doped CNTs
S1.material_description: Nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes with bamboo-like structure (thin compartment layers); nanotube diameter 50-400 nm, wall thickness 10-20 nm; synthesised by catalysed pyrolysis of melamine with FeCl3
S1.activation_method: none (no activation step; degassed/evacuated before measurement)
S1.purification_method: 0.5 M hydrochloric acid for 24 h to remove catalyst residue, then washed with deionised water several times, dried

measurements.source_location: Table 1 column 'N-doped CNTs (this work)', p. 3301 (0.21 at 1 bar); text p. 3301; abstract; isotherm Fig 5a; BET 135 m2/g and Vt 0.38 cm3/g p. 3301; method p. 3298
measurements.note_extra: 77 K, 1 bar; the body hedges about 0.21 wt% but Table 1 and the abstract state 0.21 without a qualifier and Table 1 reserves ca. for its literature columns, so uptake_bound is exact per the primary-table rule
